title: Acts Bible Quiz - Chapter 21
description: Ten questions on Acts 21: the journey to Jerusalem, the warning of Agabus, and the uproar in the temple.

questions.text: What did the disciples at Tyre say to Paul through the Spirit?
questions.explanation: They said to Paul through the Spirit that he should not go up to Jerusalem.

answers.text: That he would sail on to Rome
That he should not go up to Jerusalem
That he would soon be set free
That he should shave his head there

questions.text: In whose house at Caesarea did Paul's companions stay?
questions.explanation: They entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.

answers.text: Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple
Agabus, the prophet from Judea
James, with whom all the elders were
Philip the evangelist, one of the seven

questions.text: What did Agabus do with Paul's belt, and what did he say?
questions.explanation: Taking Paul's belt, he bound his own feet and hands and said the Holy Spirit declared that the Jews at Jerusalem would bind the owner of the belt and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.

answers.text: He bound his own feet and hands and said the belt's owner would be bound
He gave the belt back and said Paul would be set free
He laid the belt on the ground and wept over it
He wore the belt and said he would go in Paul's place

questions.text: What did Paul answer when they begged him not to go up to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Paul said he was ready not only to be bound but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

answers.text: That he would go no further than Caesarea this time
That the Spirit had not spoken to him about this at all
That he was ready to be bound and even to die for the name of the Lord Jesus
That he would return after the day of Pentecost had passed

questions.text: What had the believers in Jerusalem been told about Paul?
questions.explanation: They said he had been reported to teach the Jews among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children and not to walk after the customs.

answers.text: That he teaches the Jews among the Gentiles to forsake Moses
That he had taken money from the Gentiles
That he no longer preached the resurrection
That he had been bound already at Caesarea

questions.text: What did James and the elders tell Paul to do?
questions.explanation: They told him to take the four men who had taken a vow, purify himself with them, and pay their expenses so that they might shave their heads.

answers.text: To leave the city of Jerusalem at once and quietly
To write a letter to the Gentile believers about it
To offer a sacrifice in the temple for his own sins
To purify himself with four men under a vow and pay their expenses

questions.text: Why did the Jews from Asia stir up the multitude against Paul in the temple?
questions.explanation: They had seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city and supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.

answers.text: He had refused to pay for the purification of the men
He had spoken to the people in Greek on the stairs
They supposed he had brought Trophimus the Ephesian into the temple
He had broken the vow that he had taken earlier

questions.text: What did the commanding officer do when he came down with the soldiers?
questions.explanation: He arrested Paul and commanded him to be bound with two chains, then asked who he was and what he had done.

answers.text: He had Paul scourged there in the street
He arrested Paul and had him bound with two chains
He sent Paul away to Caesarea that night
He left Paul to the crowd and withdrew

questions.text: What did the commanding officer ask Paul as he was about to be brought into the barracks?
questions.explanation: He asked whether Paul knew Greek, and whether he was the Egyptian who had led out four thousand men of the Assassins into the wilderness.

answers.text: Whether he knew Greek, and whether he was the Egyptian
Whether he was a priest of the temple at Jerusalem
Whether he had come up to the city for the feast
Whether he was one of the four men under a vow

questions.text: What did Paul say about himself, and what did he then do from the stairs?
questions.explanation: Paul said he was a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, and when permission was given he beckoned to the people and spoke to them in the Hebrew language.

answers.text: He said he was a Roman and asked to be sent to Caesar
He said nothing and was carried into the barracks by soldiers
He said he was a Jew from Tarsus and spoke to the people in the Hebrew language
He asked the officer to send him back to Caesarea at once
